cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, is still preaching to all Israel (Deuteronomy 5:1). Now he's talking money, and he starts with a clock. At the end of every seven years, something big happens to debts.

cards.question: At the end of every seven years Israel must ___ debts.

cards.text: Every creditor cancels what he loaned to his neighbor and collects nothing from his brother. Picture opening your credit card bill and the whole thing just says NEVER MIND.

cards.question: Why does the lender stop collecting from his neighbor?

answers.text: The LORD's time of release has been proclaimed
The neighbor has already paid it back twice
The elders at the city gate have voided it

cards.question: The year of release also wipes out what a foreigner owes an Israelite.

cards.text: Then Moses says there will be no poor among them, because the LORD will surely bless them in the land He's giving them. Friend, that's a promise worth reading TWICE.

cards.question: Moses says the LORD's blessing in the land, with no poor among them, comes with a condition: Israel obeys the LORD and carefully follows His commands.
When the LORD blesses them as He promised, Israel will ___ to many nations but borrow from none, and ___ over many nations but be ruled by none.

cards.text: But if there's a poor man among their brothers, Moses says don't harden your heart or shut your hand. No going quiet in the group chat the second somebody types 'Hey, so, um…'

cards.question: Instead of shutting his hand, what is an Israelite to do for his poor brother?

answers.text: Open his hand and loan what he needs
Point him to a richer man in town
Hire him to work for one season

cards.text: Then Moses calls out a wicked thought: the seventh year, the year of release, is near. That man is looking at his brother, but he's thinking about the CALENDAR.

cards.question: What does Moses warn that wicked thought about the year of release will lead to?
Moses says the poor brother will cry out to the LORD against that man, and the man will be guilty of sin.

cards.text: So give generously, Moses says, and don't let your heart be grieved when you do. No handing it over with the face I make when I give away the LAST chocolate chip cookie.

cards.question: When an Israelite gives generously to his poor brother without a grieving heart, Moses says the LORD will ___ him in all his work.

cards.text: Then Moses says there will never cease to be poor in the land. That's why he commands them to open wide their hand to their brother and to the poor and needy in their land.
Now Moses moves from loans to servants. Say a fellow Hebrew, a man or a woman, is sold to you and serves you six years.

cards.question: In the seventh year, the master must ___ the Hebrew servant who served him six years.

cards.text: When the servant goes, Moses says don't send him away empty-handed. No six years of hard work ending with a handshake and a sad little cardboard box, friend.

cards.question: When a master frees his Hebrew servant, he sends him off with plenty from his flock, his threshing floor and his winepress. How much does he give?

answers.text: As the LORD has blessed him
One tenth of that year's harvest

cards.question: Moses gives Israel something to remember as the reason for freeing Hebrew servants and sending them off with plenty. What is it?

answers.text: They were slaves in Egypt and the LORD redeemed them
Freed servants will speak well of their old masters
The nations around them are watching how they live

cards.text: But what if the servant says, 'I do not want to leave you'? Friend, I spent years in a drawer waiting for that thing to open, and this man gets the door WIDE open and says nah, I'm good.

cards.question: Why does the Hebrew servant tell his master he doesn't want to leave?

answers.text: He loves his master and household and is well off
He has no family left to go home to
He still owes his master money from a loan

cards.text: Then the master takes an awl and pierces it through the servant's ear into the door.

cards.question: When a Hebrew servant chooses to stay with his master, how long does he become his servant?

answers.text: For the rest of his life
Until the next year of release

cards.question: Moses says a maidservant who chooses to stay is treated a different way from a manservant.

cards.text: Moses tells them not to regard it as a hardship to set a servant free. And he's got the math to back it up.

cards.question: Moses says a freed Hebrew servant's six years of service were worth ___ the wages of a hired hand.
Moses says every firstborn male from Israel's herds and flocks must be set apart to the LORD their God.

cards.text: Every firstborn ox stays off the job and every firstborn sheep keeps its wool, and each year the household eats the firstborn before the LORD at the place He will choose. A firstborn with a defect, like one that's lame or blind, isn't sacrificed to the LORD. They eat that one within their gates, the ceremonially clean and unclean alike, but they don't eat the blood. They pour it on the ground like water.
And that's where we'll set this batch down for now. Keep that apron on, friend, because Moses is NOT done preaching.
